• Selectively giving exam information to some students.
• Negligence in keeping exam materials secure. | *Rule 1 – Examination Leakage (Staff)* | | | **Negligent invigilation** | • Reading newspapers or other material during an exam.
• Leaving the exam room without arranging an alternative invigilator.
• Arriving late for invigilation.
• Failing to report malpractice promptly.
• Not actively monitoring the exam room or candidates, or failing to secure the candidate’s signature. | *Rule 2 – Negligent invigilation (Staff)* | | | **Refusal to invigilate** | • (Details not fully provided in the excerpt, but listed as a separate offence.) | *Rule 3 – Refusal to invigilate (Staff)* | | **Student‑related** | **Malpractices in relation to coursework** | • Giving another student prepared coursework to help them complete their own.
• Negligently exposing one’s coursework to another student for use. | *Rule 1 – Malpractices in Relation to Coursework* | | | **Fraud in relation to coursework** | • Submitting coursework that was not prepared by the student.
• Substantially plagiarising. | *Rule 2 – Fraud in Relation to Coursework* | **Summary** Examination malpractice at Makerere includes any of the following: 1. **For staff** – leaking exam information, being negligent or refusing to invigilate, or otherwise failing to secure the integrity of the examination process. 2. **For students** – providing or using another’s coursework, submitting work that is not their own, or plagiarising.
